source_text: Homines Dei opus esse defendimus nec ex illius potentia vel in malum vel in bonum invitum aliquem cogi, sed propria voluntate aut bonum facere aut malum, in bono vero opere a Dei gratia semper adiuvari, in malum vero diaboli suggestionibus incitari.
pass_a_gloss: We defend that human beings are God's work, and that no one unwilling is forced by His power either into evil or into good, but by his own will does either good or evil; in a good work always helped by God's grace, but toward evil stirred by the devil's suggestions.

lemmas.lexica: LS malum; Blaise malum naturale vs malum voluntatis
LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will
LS gratia=favor; Blaise grace; in iustitia definitions often 'favoritism'

pass_b_english: We maintain that human beings are God's work. His power does not force anyone against their will into either evil or good. People do good or evil by their own will. In a good action they are always helped by God's grace; toward evil they are urged by the devil's suggestions.

choices.why: Julian's definition of sin is an act of will. Keep 'will' rather than later 'free will' system language unless liberum arbitrium is present.
Augustine's quoted claim that the unbaptized remain under the devil; keep the personal devil, not 'evil'.
rejected: under Satan (name not in the Latin here)

choices.why: In the suum cuique definition gratia is partiality, not saving grace.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (Letter to Rome, words preserved in Augustine, Contra duas epistolas Pelagianorum 1); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
